newsitem.title: UK: RUGBY UNION-SCOTLAND RECALL TAIT FOR IRELAND CLASH.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-SCOTLAND RECALL TAIT FOR IRELAND CLASH.

text.p: Fly-half Craig Chalmers and former rugby league player Alan Tait were named on Tuesday in the Scotland side to play Ireland in the Five Nations championship at Murrayfield on Saturday.

Tait, who won eight caps for Scotland in 1987 and 1988 before switching to rugby league, will play in the centre alongside Gregor Townsend whose move from fly-half is one of four positional changes to the team beaten 41-6 by England at Twickenham.

The other changes see Tony Stanger returning to the right wing from centre and, in the pack, captain Rob Wainwright returning to his preferred position of blindside flank and Peter Walton switching to number eight.

Scotland: Rowen Shepherd; Tony Stanger, Alan Tait, Gregor Townsend, Kenny Logan; Craig Chalmers, Bryan Redpath; Peter Walton, Ian Smith, Rob Wainwright (captain), Andy Reed, Doddie Weir, Mattie Stewart, Graham Ellis, Tom Smith.
